facts.statement: The type species Baurutitan britoi was officially described in 2005 by Kellner and colleagues, even though the fossils were discovered in 1957.
facts.quote: The type species, Baurutitan britoi, was described in 2005 by Kellner and colleagues, although the fossil remains had already been discovered in 1957.

facts.statement: The holotype of Baurutitan was found in 1957 by the Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price in the Peirópolis region of Minas Gerais.
facts.quote: The holotype of Baurutitan were found in 1957 by Llewellyn Ivor Price, the famous Brazilian paleontologist, in the region of Peirópolis, Minas Gerais.

facts.statement: Price conducted excavations at an old quarry known as Quarry Caieira on the São Luis farm.
facts.quote: Price then conducted excavations in an old quarry, known as Quarry Caieira, on the in São Luis farm.

facts.statement: Excavations at Quarry Caieira recovered fossils of turtles, crocodylomorphs, theropods, sauropods, fish, freshwater invertebrates, trace fossils, egg fragments, and plant debris.
facts.quote: Recovered fossils included those of turtles, crocodylomorphs, theropods and sauropods, fish, freshwater invertebrates (gastropods and bivalves), trace fossils, fragments of eggs, and plant debris.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a series of 19 vertebrae, including the last sacral and 18 caudals, which were initially named 'Series C' before becoming the holotype of Baurutitan.
facts.quote: A series of 19 vertebrae (the last sacral and 18 caudals) found at this locality were recognized as belong to those of a titanosaur; they were initially named 'Series "C"', and subsequently became the holotype of the new genus Baurutitan (specimen number MCT 1490-R).

facts.statement: All recovered fossil material is stored in the collection of the Earth Science Museum (MCT) in Rio de Janeiro.
facts.quote: All material found was stored in the collection of Museu de Ciência da Terra (Earth Science Museum – MCT) of the Departamento Nacional de Produção Mineral (National Department of Mineral Production) in Rio de Janeiro.

facts.statement: Baurutitan fossils were found in the Serra da Galga Formation near Uberaba in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais.
facts.quote: This South American dinosaur was found in the Serra da Galga Formation near Uberaba, in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the Maastrichtian epoch, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was found in the Serra da Galga Formation, dating to the Maastrichtian epoch, some 72-66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Baurutitan was estimated to be 12 to 14 meters long and about 3.5 meters tall.
facts.quote: Baurutitan was a sauropod which was estimated to have measured 12 - 14 m long and had a height of around 3.5 m.

facts.statement: Baurutitan was a large long-necked herbivorous sauropod estimated to be between 12 and 16 meters long and about 3.5 meters tall.
facts.quote: Baurutitan era un saurópodo, un gran herbívoro de cuello largo, que se calcula que medía entre 12-16 metros de largo y tenía una altura de alrededor de 3,5 metros.

facts.statement: Baurutitan belongs to the unranked family Titanosauria.
The name Baurutitan combines 'bauru', referring to the geographical region, and 'titan' from Greek myths, while 'britoi' honors Brazilian paleontologist Ignacio Aureliano Brito Machado.
facts.quote: El nombre Baurutitan proviene de la unión de la palabra "bauru", que alude a la región geográfica del hallazgo, dentro del Grupo Bauru y la palabra titan de los mitos griegos; britoi se da en honor a Ignacio Aureliano Brito Machado (1938-2001), un paleontólogo brasileño que aconsejó el estudio y la descripción de este dinosaurio, cuyos fósiles han permanecido almacenados durante muchos años.

facts.statement: Baurutitan was the fourth sauropod described in Brazil, following Antarctosaurus, Gondwanatitan, and Amazonsaurus.
facts.quote: Baurutitan fue el cuarto saurópodo descrito en Brasil, después de Antarctosaurus, Gondwanatitan y Amazonsaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Marilia Formation, dating to the Maastrichtian epoch, about 72 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen del holotipo fue encontrado en la formación de Marilia, que data a la época de Maastrichtiano, hace unos 72-66 millones de años.

facts.statement: Baurutitan lived during the Maastrichtian epoch, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
